report.verdict: Cobalt Pay is looking for an engineering manager, while your experience is in home services operations. I’d pass on this particular fit because the resume doesn’t show engineering management or backend engineering. Your operations leadership deserves a fuller account for roles in that field.
write_up: Cobalt Pay’s role is a different track from the one your resume shows. Your progression from Lakeland Appliance Repair to Senior Director at Northstar Home Services points to operations leadership. It’s common for senior resumes to list responsibilities this way, but without team or budget figures and results, a recruiter can’t compare the work with other operations leaders in the pile.

The line about partnering with Finance on the annual operating plan is your best model: it names the partner and the work. Your progression at Northstar is easy to follow, but the current role leaves the scale of your leadership and what changed under it open.

Let’s start with the first line under Senior Director. Add the number of people and the budget you were responsible for, if you can confirm them, then name the initiatives and results behind the rest of the role. For Cobalt Pay, add relevant technical experience only if you have it.

cards.line: The resume does not say how large Northstar Home Services is.
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter may not know Northstar. A company-wide employee count would give them a frame for the regional operation you lead.
cards.question: How many employees does Northstar Home Services have?

cards.line: Responsible for field operations, dispatch and customer care across the Upper Midwest
cards.cannot_tell: The geography is clear, but a recruiter can’t tell how many people or how much budget came with the remit. Those figures matter for a senior operations role.
cards.example: Responsible for field operations, dispatch and customer care across the Upper Midwest, with [number of employees] and an operating budget of [amount]
cards.question: How many people and how much operating budget were you responsible for?

cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can’t tell what you handled with vendors or how large the fleet was. Both help show what this part of the job involved.
cards.example: Oversaw vendor management for [vendor work] and a fleet of [number] vehicles
cards.question: What vendor work did you oversee, and how many vehicles were in the fleet?

cards.line: Led operational strategy and continuous improvement initiatives
cards.cannot_tell: This doesn’t name an initiative or what changed. Pick one a recruiter can connect to the field operation.
cards.example: Led [initiative] as part of operational strategy and continuous improvement, resulting in [what changed]
cards.question: Which initiative did you lead, and what changed?

cards.cannot_tell: Managing managers is important at this level, but the line doesn’t say how many or what their teams handled.
cards.example: Managed [number] managers across multiple regions whose teams handled [work]
cards.question: How many managers did you manage, and what did their teams handle?

cards.line: Oversaw technicians and dispatch for the Twin Cities market
cards.cannot_tell: The work and market are named, but the number of technicians and dispatch staff is missing.
cards.example: Oversaw [number] technicians and [number] dispatch staff for the Twin Cities market
cards.question: How many technicians and dispatch staff did you oversee?

cards.line: Rolled out a new scheduling system
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can see you rolled it out, but not who used it or what changed after the rollout.
cards.example: Rolled out a new scheduling system for [users], resulting in [what changed]
cards.question: Who used the new system, and what changed after the rollout?

cards.cannot_tell: This names a useful service measure, but not how you improved it or how much it moved.
cards.example: Improved first-time fix rate from [starting rate] to [ending rate] by [action]
cards.question: What did you do to improve first-time fix rate, and what were the starting and ending rates?

cards.line: Ran daily operations for the service department
cards.cannot_tell: Daily operations could cover a lot of work. Name the responsibilities that were yours and how many people were involved.
cards.example: Ran daily operations for the service department, including [responsibilities] for [number] staff
cards.question: Which responsibilities did you handle, and how many staff were in the department?

cards.cannot_tell: Hiring and training are clear, but the number of technicians and what the training covered are still open.
cards.example: Hired and trained [number] technicians in [training topics]
cards.question: How many technicians did you hire and train, and what did the training cover?

cards.line: Reported to the COO and partnered with Finance on the annual operating plan
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model for naming the people you worked with and the concrete plan you worked on.

fit.why: Your headline and your progression at Northstar both point to senior operations leadership.
fit.level: director, manages managers across multiple regions
fit.note: Your regional operations leadership and partnership with Finance relate to parts of Cobalt Pay’s day-to-day work. If you have relevant technical experience not shown here, put it in the experience section.

posting.summary: Cobalt Pay seeks an engineering manager to lead backend engineers responsible for payouts and the ledger.
missing: 2+ years managing engineers with direct reports, including hiring and performance management
5+ years of backend engineering before moving into management
Experience leading teams that run production systems with on-call
A record of growing engineers into senior roles
